title: NSE’s IPO in numbers: How India’s biggest exchange stacks up on scale and earnings- Moneycontrol.com
text:
My Alerts Go Ad-Free Follow us on: The NSE’s IPO comes at a time when India’s capital markets have expanded sharply, with rising market capitalisation, trading activity and passive fund assets.   September 16, 2026 / 16:15 IST             NSE’s numbers offer a snapshot of the exchange’s scale, profitability and growing role in India’s capital markets ahead of its proposed IPO. From a larger listed-company base and rising passive fund assets to strong derivatives activity and improving operating margins, the data highlights how the exchange has evolved across trading, listings and indices. NSE’s operating metrics show a steady expansion in its listed universe and the ecosystem built around its benchmark Nifty indices. The number of listed entities on the exchange rose to 3,005 in Q1 FY27, compared with 2,978 at the end of FY26 and 2,719 in FY25. The market capitalisation of listed companies also increased to Rs 474 lakh crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 411 lakh crore in FY26. The exchange has also seen sustained growth in passive investing linked to its indices. Total assets under management of India’s passive funds linked to Nifty indices stood at Rs 9 lakh crore in Q1 FY27, up from Rs 8 lakh crore in FY26 and Rs 6.3 lakh crore in FY24. NSE continues to command significant trading activity across cash equities, futures and options. Cash market average daily traded value (ADTV) stood at Rs 1.36 lakh crore in Q1 FY27, up from Rs 1.06 lakh crore in FY26. Equity futures ADTV, however, moderated to Rs 1.59 lakh crore in FY26 from Rs 1.86 lakh crore in FY25. Options remain the biggest part of NSE’s trading ecosystem by notional value. Equity options notional value stood at nearly Rs 249.2 lakh crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 258.3 lakh crore in FY26. On a premium-value basis, however, activity increased to Rs 64,352 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 57,662 crore in FY26. NSE reported revenue from operations of Rs 4,560 crore in Q1 FY27, taking total income to Rs 5,252 crore. Revenue from operations for FY26 stood at Rs 16,601 crore, lower than Rs 17,141 crore in FY25, while total income was broadly stable at Rs 18,713 crore compared with Rs 19,177 crore in FY25. Profitability, however, improved sharply in the June quarter. NSE’s operating EBITDA margin stood at 78.8% in Q1 FY27, significantly higher than the 66.9% reported for FY26 and 73.8% in FY25. Profit after tax came in at Rs 3,120 crore during the quarter. For the full year FY26, PAT stood at Rs 10,302 crore, down from Rs 12,188 crore in FY25 and Rs 8,306 crore in FY24. NSE’s listing data reflects the continued depth of India’s primary and capital markets. The exchange saw eight mainboard IPOs and 14 SME IPOs in Q1 FY27. For the full year, FY26 recorded 108 mainboard IPOs and 111 SME listings, while FY25 saw 79 mainboard and 163 SME IPOs. Total equity raised through the exchange stood at Rs 1.3 lakh crore in Q1 FY27. Across FY26, companies raised Rs 4.8 lakh crore through equity, compared with Rs 4.5 lakh crore in FY25 and Rs 2.4 lakh crore in FY24. Debt mobilisation remains significantly larger than equity fundraising. Companies raised Rs 4.9 lakh crore through debt in Q1 FY27, while total debt raised stood at Rs 15.6 lakh crore in FY26. Overall fund mobilisation through equity and debt reached Rs 6.2 lakh crore in the June quarter, compared with Rs 20.3 lakh crore during FY26. NSE’s valuation at the time of its proposed public-market listing compares with a higher multiple assigned to its listed peer, BSE, based on FY26 financials. The table shows NSE at a price-to-earnings multiple of 42.9 times, compared with 54.28 times for BSE. The comparison provides a reference point for investors assessing the valuation at which NSE is seeking to enter the public markets. Both exchanges have benefited from the structural growth in India’s capital markets, particularly the expansion of retail participation and derivatives trading. The NSE’s IPO comes at a time when India’s capital markets have expanded sharply, with rising market capitalisation, trading activity and passive fund assets.

September 16, 2026 / 16:15 IST

NSE’s numbers offer a snapshot of the exchange’s scale, profitability and growing role in India’s capital markets ahead of its proposed IPO. From a larger listed-company base and rising passive fund assets to strong derivatives activity and improving operating margins, the data highlights how the exchange has evolved across trading, listings and indices.

NSE’s operating metrics show a steady expansion in its listed universe and the ecosystem built around its benchmark Nifty indices. The number of listed entities on the exchange rose to 3,005 in Q1 FY27, compared with 2,978 at the end of FY26 and 2,719 in FY25. The market capitalisation of listed companies also increased to Rs 474 lakh crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 411 lakh crore in FY26.

The exchange has also seen sustained growth in passive investing linked to its indices. Total assets under management of India’s passive funds linked to Nifty indices stood at Rs 9 lakh crore in Q1 FY27, up from Rs 8 lakh crore in FY26 and Rs 6.3 lakh crore in FY24.

NSE continues to command significant trading activity across cash equities, futures and options. Cash market average daily traded value (ADTV) stood at Rs 1.36 lakh crore in Q1 FY27, up from Rs 1.06 lakh crore in FY26. Equity futures ADTV, however, moderated to Rs 1.59 lakh crore in FY26 from Rs 1.86 lakh crore in FY25.

Options remain the biggest part of NSE’s trading ecosystem by notional value. Equity options notional value stood at nearly Rs 249.2 lakh crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 258.3 lakh crore in FY26. On a premium-value basis, however, activity increased to Rs 64,352 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 57,662 crore in FY26.

NSE reported revenue from operations of Rs 4,560 crore in Q1 FY27, taking total income to Rs 5,252 crore. Revenue from operations for FY26 stood at Rs 16,601 crore, lower than Rs 17,141 crore in FY25, while total income was broadly stable at Rs 18,713 crore compared with Rs 19,177 crore in FY25.

Profitability, however, improved sharply in the June quarter. NSE’s operating EBITDA margin stood at 78.8% in Q1 FY27, significantly higher than the 66.9% reported for FY26 and 73.8% in FY25. Profit after tax came in at Rs 3,120 crore during the quarter.

For the full year FY26, PAT stood at Rs 10,302 crore, down from Rs 12,188 crore in FY25 and Rs 8,306 crore in FY24.

NSE’s listing data reflects the continued depth of India’s primary and capital markets. The exchange saw eight mainboard IPOs and 14 SME IPOs in Q1 FY27.

For the full year, FY26 recorded 108 mainboard IPOs and 111 SME listings, while FY25 saw 79 mainboard and 163 SME IPOs.

Total equity raised through the exchange stood at Rs 1.3 lakh crore in Q1 FY27. Across FY26, companies raised Rs 4.8 lakh crore through equity, compared with Rs 4.5 lakh crore in FY25 and Rs 2.4 lakh crore in FY24.

Debt mobilisation remains significantly larger than equity fundraising. Companies raised Rs 4.9 lakh crore through debt in Q1 FY27, while total debt raised stood at Rs 15.6 lakh crore in FY26. Overall fund mobilisation through equity and debt reached Rs 6.2 lakh crore in the June quarter, compared with Rs 20.3 lakh crore during FY26.

NSE’s valuation at the time of its proposed public-market listing compares with a higher multiple assigned to its listed peer, BSE, based on FY26 financials. The table shows NSE at a price-to-earnings multiple of 42.9 times, compared with 54.28 times for BSE.

The comparison provides a reference point for investors assessing the valuation at which NSE is seeking to enter the public markets. Both exchanges have benefited from the structural growth in India’s capital markets, particularly the expansion of retail participation and derivatives trading.
